profile.headline: Software Engineer at Facebook
profile.summary: Software engineer with experience in firmware, networking, and embedded systems. Interested in all things systems related, both big and small.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Co-designed and implemented new MCU software architecture on top of FreeRTOS for two new SoC based IoT products
• Conducted hardware bringup and validation (EVT to PVT) and supported factory tests for two new SoC boards: Arm Cortex M4 MCU with SPI, CAN, USB, RS-485, ADC, accelerometer, among other peripherals
• Developed features for the Vehicle Gateway, spanning firmware (Linux environment writing mostly Go code) to backend (Go), leveraging vehicle data to give customers new insights into their fleet
• Collaborated cross team (hardware, firmware, backend, PM, management) to develop features, hardware, and to win several multi-million dollar deals
• Led small group that analyzed vehicle bus traffic (CAN, SW-CAN, KLine)for useful data, eventually spun off into a full team
• Developed new techniques to analyze automotive CAN bus for diagnostic data

projects.title: Multi-Paxos Implementation
projects.description: Implemented Multi-Paxos for a chat program as part of EECS 591 - Distributed Systems.

projects.title: Home IoT Hub Replication: The Practicality of SpecPaxos and NOPaxos in a Single Switch Environment
projects.description: Replication increases the availability of critical systems and is implemented through algorithms such as Paxos. With the advent of the smart home and along with it mission critical embedded devices, their availability has become increasingly important. A large number of these embedded devices rely on a centralized hub. In this paper, we show that novel replication protocols that are codesigned with specific networks in mind, such as SpecPaxos and NOPaxos with data centers, can be adapted to the home network environment for hub replication and continue to provide performance improvements. Among these replication protocols, our evaluation shows that NOPaxos emerges as the lowest latency and highest throughput system, with a request latency of 1.6 milliseconds and throughput of 10689 requests per second.
